faqs.question: What is the Ultrasonic Cleaner used for?
faqs.answer: It's used for fast, thorough cleaning of dental instruments, orthodontic appliances, and prosthetic devices via ultrasonic cavitation in a heated bath.

faqs.question: How does ultrasonic cleaning remove biofilm?
faqs.answer: Ultrasonic agitation dislodges and removes biofilm buildup from instrument surfaces, reaching contamination that manual brushing typically misses.

faqs.question: Which model fits a small practice versus a busy clinic?
faqs.answer: INK50-SK2 (2.5 L) suits individual instruments or small batches, INK150-SK2 (5.7 L) fits moderate daily volume, and INK200-SK2 (12 L) covers full-tray or high-volume clinical use.

faqs.question: What heating range does the cleaner support?
faqs.answer: Ambient temperature up to 80°C, adjustable to match the material being cleaned.

faqs.question: How long does a cleaning cycle take?
faqs.answer: Cycle time is adjustable from 5 to 60 minutes depending on contamination level.

faqs.question: What frequency do these units run at?
faqs.answer: 40 kHz across all three models.

faqs.question: Does the cleaner include a drain outlet?
faqs.answer: Yes, all models include a discharge outlet for easy tank draining, along with a carry handle.

faqs.question: Is ultrasonic cleaning safe for delicate appliances like orthodontic devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, cavitation-based cleaning is gentler than manual scrubbing, reducing the risk of damage to braces, retainers, and aligners.

faqs.question: Does ultrasonic cleaning replace sterilization?
faqs.answer: No, it supports and improves sterilization outcomes by thoroughly pre-cleaning instruments before the sterilization step.

longForm.heroHook: Reaches the joint, the hinge, the serration, everywhere a brush can't go.
longForm.heroLead: Manual scrubbing cleans what the brush can physically reach. Blood, saliva, and biofilm settle into the places it can't, the pin joints on forceps, the serrations on scalers, the fine channels inside a handpiece and stay there through cycle after cycle of visible-clean instruments. Ultrasonic cavitation doesn't have that limit. Sound waves at 40 kHz generate microscopic bubbles that collapse against every surface a solution touches, dislodging contamination from geometry a brush never contacts. Three tank sizes — 2.5 L, 5.7 L, and 12 L — cover everything from a single instrument between patients to a full clinical tray, with heating from ambient to 80°C and cycle times adjustable from 5 to 60 minutes to match how dirty the load actually is. Every model ships with a carry handle and a discharge outlet, so moving it and draining it are never the bottleneck. The result reaches deeper than manual cleaning, protects delicate instruments better than abrasive scrubbing does, and gives sterilization a genuinely clean surface to work from.

sections.title: Overview
body: Ultrasonic cleaning removes contaminants thoroughly, providing a clean, hygienic environment for the next use of an instrument or device.
In dental and clinical workflows specifically, it strengthens infection control, improves patient safety, and extends the working life of instruments exposed to repeated cleaning cycles.
The dental industry applies ultrasonic baths across cleaning and maintaining dental instruments, sterilization support, biofilm removal, and cleaning orthodontic and prosthodontic appliances.
Three models cover different volume needs: INK50-SK2 (2.5 L), INK150-SK2 (5.7 L), and INK200-SK2 (12 L), all running at 40 kHz.
Heating ranges from ambient up to 80°C across all models, with adjustable cycle times from 5 to 60 minutes.
All three models include a handle for portability and a discharge outlet for easy tank draining.

longForm.heroHook: One bath. Cleaning, degassing, and dispersion, without switching equipment.
longForm.heroLead: A pharma or materials lab rarely needs just cleaning. The same bench often needs dissolved gas pulled out of a formulation before it's tested, trapped air cleared from a coating before it's analysed, or a manufacturing tool degreased before the next run — three different jobs that, done separately, mean three different pieces of equipment. The Ultrasonic Bath does all three from one tank. Dual 40/80 kHz frequency on every model means the same cavitation that clears grease from a pump or valve also accelerates gas release from solutions, suspensions, and emulsions — improving formulation stability without a separate degassing step. Power is adjustable from 10% to 100%, so intensity scales from a gentle pass on a delicate sample to full-strength cleaning on a stubborn residue, and heating runs from ambient to 100°C across a 0 to 99 minute cycle window. Four tank sizes — 4.3 L through 22 L — scale from small-batch sample prep to production-scale pharmaceutical processing, each with the same handle-and-discharge convenience as the rest of the range.
